scars-of-kalakar/lore/0---the-lost-era/0.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/0 - The Lost Era/0000-00-00.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/0---the-lost-era/0.content:
Molania, a barren wasteland akin to Mars, beckoned the Lost Ones with the promise of transformation. The mission commenced with hope, as domed cities dotted the planet’s surface, each acting as a crucial node for the colossal Terran Incubator. However, fate had other plans.
Molania’s long, hot days made it a haven for solar farms—until the sandstorms struck. A meteor had struck the planet, disrupting the weather.
The relentless storms ravaged the solar panels, rendering them obsolete and plunging the SEED into a state of desperation. Communication lines fell silent, and the grand vision of Terra-forming crumbled.
Daylight ceased to exist. A neighboring planet’s orbit cast an unrelenting shadow, blocking the star’s life-giving warmth. Panic stirred, but scientists reassured that it would pass within months. 
Desperation led to a grim decision: the order was given to the robotic servants to decommission the project. The planet, once alive with ambition, fell into an eerie stillness.
There were no cries, there were no screams, just silence. Then darkness.
Over millennia, a massive meteor slammed into the planet, landing perilously close to a SEED, engulfing it under its weight. Comprised predominantly of frozen oxygen and nitrogen, along with new elements, the meteor began to dissolve, releasing torrents of rain that enveloped the planet. This flooded the lands, resulting in a sole continent.
This influx of nutrient-rich elements accelerated evolution, resulting in the emergence of new species. Among them, some began to develop sapience.
Kalakar - unscarred.png
1642-04-01

scars-of-kalakar/lore/1---discovery-era/.content:
Sapient races encounter each other for the first time
Kalakains when leaving the desert, were heading out to conquer the lands, believing it was their right as an Empirialist society.  They came across other villages, and were surprised they could communicate. At first they believed other Kalakains domesticated and taught these species. Realizing they fooled themselves, they make treaties to trade, otherwise they will go to war.
Elegin, Toulikour,  Junkofuya, Burlian, Kralerian, Drengar, Muri  Equu and Kalakain all join the treaty
Kalakar - discovery.png
1652-06-10

Kingdom of Kalakar established
Capitalist Economy
First coinage (Silver)
the Kingdom of the Kalakains stood as the first great civilization, a beacon of unity that brought together a multitude of cultures, naming the lands after themselves; Kalakar. They established the earliest trade routes, weaving a network of commerce that spanned from East to West.
They also were able to use the plentiful hot springs for steam power, launching into the first Great Civilization.
The Elegin, wise in the ways of nature, worked as advisors.
The Kalakains, viewing themselves as superior to other races, sowed the seeds of their own downfall. Greed and corruption seeped into the heart of their society, eroding the foundations of their empire from within. Despite the grandeur of their open roads facilitating trade, the kingdom ultimately crumbled under the weight of its own hubris.
1692-11-29

A member of the king’s advisors wanted to sell cheap tonics and potions, but could not compete with Magika Vitalis. He began a PR campaign to get it banned, stating its unnatural, witchraft, and makes people careless. Kalakains believing Magika Vitalis is against nature through propaganda, outlawed performing Magika Vitalis. This caused the Elegin to retreat to the west, and separate from the kingdom.
1693-09-17

With poor quality medicines, sold at exorbitant prices. Disease begins to spread fast. Famine spreads as farmers catch sick. Over time trust in the Court wears thin.
1703-01-04

Kalakains in a final cling to power, declares martial law and control of the Kingdom, and removes all other races from advisory roles.
1713-02-06

Greed and corruption caused even Kalakains to disregard the court, and the Kingdom loses the last of its power. Merchants continue to use trades routes established and slowly rise to power.
1718-06-07
1718-08-07

scars-of-kalakar/lore/2---guilded-age/17.content:
Merchants create the first Guild, followed by a craftsman guild, and an engineering guild. The Guilds rise in power and status, with the Merchant Guild being the strongest.
Barter economy, with prices set by the guilds each month. Leads to a Fraternist society.
Kalakar - guilded.png
1733-11-02

Drengar, feeling discriminated by the guilds, extorted by price gouging, and being underpaid, due to their size and intelligence, go into isolation.
Economically, this causes a famine the guilds try to hide as there are no Drengar to till the fields, or other hard labors.
The bakers begin using sawdust in the bread, engineers used iron nails instead of steel, 
1753-10-02

Desperate, the guilds reach out to the Elegin where they share their technology of farming, irrigation, and wells. Saving the continent from famine.
The Elegin, having been in isolation, opens their borders for the first time, allowing trade of textiles and spices.
The economy moves to a gold based economy.
1762-09-30

Burlians angry at being cheated by the Junkofuya craft guilds, raids territory/tradepost ran by the guild.
The merchant guild ignored the Junkofuya as they were the weapon makers, and should be able to defend themselves.
1767-03-16

Burlians and Junkofuya are in a stalemate. The Burlians are adaptive hunters, and got used to the jungle. Using guerrilla tactics, the Junkofuya are forced into the swamp lands of the highly territorial Drengar.
1767-08-14

Fighting a two front war, the Junkofuya are nearly driven to extinction. Their population shrank from 400,000 to nearly 50,000 accounted for.
1768-01-01
Toulikours, a nation of warriors, decided they were weighed down by too much bureaucracy and dissolved their government. They decide to become nomads and mercenaries.

the Rastarians, driven from their mountainous homeland by overcrowding and dwindling resources, descended into the lowlands. Viewed as outsiders and treated akin to gypsies, as they brought new diseases, they soon fell under the yoke of the Kalakains, who captured and enslaved them.
Seeking refuge and protection, the Rastarians forged an alliance with the Drengar, offering priceless gems and arms in exchange for their security. They form the KOA
Meanwhile, the Elegin Toulikour and Junkofuya entered into a pact named Waron to defend against any potential aggression from the KOA forces, ensuring a fragile balance of power in the region.
1772-05-13

Rastarian Consulate member is assassinated by Empirialists
1772-05-30

Rastarians raid Kalakain villages in retaliation. Waron refuse to act as to not battle KOA
The Rastarians then show their true power. Using blood magiq called Magika Sanguis; they begin retaliation against the Kalakains
Drengar then come out of isolation, and in honoring the treaty, both Rastarians and Drengar begin raiding and kidnapping Kalakains, and freeing Rastarian slaves. Aberdine Salazar Abacus is kidnapped during a raid in his home village.
This came as a surprise to the Waron, as they were assisting the Junkofuya to fend of the Burlians from the North. They left little to guard their homelands. The Junkofuya that were pushed into the swamp lands were slaughtered by the KOA. 
KOA then march West. One of the few survivors, Zed Trice, follows in pursuit.
1772-06-19

It took 2 weeks for the word of the annihilation to reach Dmascus Maktar, Pharaoh of the Elegin.
Ha’Ven Maktar pleads to his father, Dmascus Maktar, to take the diplomatic route, against the word of his advisor , Ha’Ven Maktar states he will fight for what is right, and is jailed.
Rastarians reach out to the Burlian army, and they join the KOA
Through tunnels and routes through the mountains were more efficient and quickly adavanced through the mountainous territory, having an advantage over the top dwellers.
1772-06-24

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-06-24.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
The KOA arrive in the western lowlands, and blitzkrieg through farmers, and poorly manned outposts. They begin enchanting creatures of the forests and fields to join their fight.
Dmascus Maktar orders his Heralds to defend the capital. and orders the rest of his army to defend the isthmus of the peninsula.
1772-07-02

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-07-02.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
The KOA slow their advance as they spread wide across the lowlands. They do not know the area. The Kralerian tribes spy from above, feeding intel to nearby soldiers and Viziers.
Intel from Toulikour spies on the front-line report the use of new Magika Sanguis, and even stole tomes and spells from the Rastarians lazy in their advance and not cleaning up camps.
Creed Billingstone out of protest against the War, that diplomacy is the way, vacates the Consulate, and introduces himself to Dmascus Maktar but is rejected because he is the enemy.
Aberdine Salazar Abacus discovers Electra, Abacus convinces the Consulate to let him research.
Dmascus Maktar orders his Hemet to learn of the new magika, and how they can use it. They required sources of blood to study the spells and tomes, Dmascus Maktar offers Ha’Ven Maktar. Creed Billingstone to shorten Ha’Ven Maktar suffering decides to reveal the secrets to the Hemet to speed up research.
1772-07-19

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-07-19.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
The war enters a stalemate, the KOA are held back due to coordination between the Toulikour, Elegin, Kralerian and Kalakain forces.
Desperate to end the war, as paying the Burlians and Drengar is getting expensive, the Rastarians chose to transform all the enslaved male Kalakains into vampire thralls using Magika Sanguis, and let them feed on the women and children. They became The Pale. Puppets to the Rastarians. No longer requiring food or sleep, mining production increases. 
Unwilling to kill innocents to empower their Darq magi, the Hemet turned to using Ha’Ven Maktar blood to infuse Magik/Darq Magi/Artifact with formidable powers as they believed his blood was godly as he was the son of the pharaoh.
Zed Trice arrives at the headquarters the KOA are coordinating the war at deep in the mountains. An underground fortress. He stakes out the area for a few days.
1772-07-20

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-07-20.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
The day was quiet, neither side attacking. The Elegin and Toulikour were weary, but the Kalakain and Kralerian believed the KOA have exhausted their resources and are retreating back to the mountains.
Some forces push back into the lowlands to survey the damage.
Seeing no threat, they spread the message to regroup, and gather the dead.
As the sun sets, the greenish skies fade to a black fog descending the mountains. Thick and unyielding. Creatures run from it, but unable to outrun it.
The Pale had descended over the lowlands, and the isthmus of the peninsula.
It took only a single night. The Rastarians waited until nightfall and unleashed their ravenous horde. They moved in shadows, slaughtering ruthlessly to quell the Hunger.
The Elegin were decimated, every Kalakain either dead or missing; driven to their city gates, but the Rastarians did not attack further, as overfeeding The Pale could give them enough strength to overpower their masters.
The Drengar, superstitious and afraid, Retreats. The Rastarians let them go, they served their purpose, and could be useful again. The Burlians pledge legion.
1772-07-22

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-07-22.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
The land was as quiet as the dead. Corpses for isles, drained of blood, not even the Mortifago partake of the fetid meat. The Elegin hide behind their city walls, afraid and broken.
Dmascus Maktar convenes with the Hemet with his most trusted Vizier Flea McCallister as the citizens are revolting, and even most of his Heralds abandoned him.
The Artifacts they created so far were sent out in battle, and are strewn across the battlefield.
They had one last Artifact, a gauntlet, made to hold the daemon Dyxe. 
Ha’Ven Maktar having been stabbed and drained repeatedly was too weak to make more. Flea McCallister begs Dmascus Maktar to stop.
Dmascus Maktar pleased with the result, order the release of Ha’Ven Maktar.
Dmascus orders Ha’Ven Maktar to put the gauntlet on. Ha’Ven refuses. Dmascus rips off Ha’Ven’s horns and orders him again. He refuses again and is beaten. He has 3 days or he will be put to death.
Zed Trice finally sees an opening and breaks inside the Rastarian stronghold. He soon runs into Aberdine Salazar Abacus who invented a power generator and lazer blaster with the Electra he found. The Consulate then takes all of Abacus’s research and sends it to the front lines. The KOA having regrouped without the Drengar push back into the lowlands.
Abacus and Zed, look around to see if they can reverse the curse set upon the Kalakain. As with most afflictions of Darq magi, it is irreversible without the use of Ghould. No time to make any, Abacus learns the Consulate member all have Ghould totems. Zed Trice figures out a way to steal the items, while Abacus prepares his Nova Generator to overload and explode, destroying the whole headquarters.
1772-07-25

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-07-25.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
Working through the night, Aberdine Salazar Abacus and Zed Trice accomplished thier tasks, and begin their escape. Abacus, while fleeing, drops a piece of Ghould. Zed picks it up, just as the explosion tears through the mountains. The first Void-out. Abacus drastically under-estimated its range and destruction.
At the edge of his feet, a vast crevasse, and his only friend gone. Abacus sees the sky once again. Overwhelmed, he falls to his knees. The headquarters for the KOA was gone.
Samuel Wibblebrook, suspicious of the silence from headquarters, sends scouts who report back the destruction. At the same time, the blueprints for the Nova Generator and Casters. Seeing this as a sign, orders their manufacture. This will turn the tides. He orders his forces to attack the Elegin capital.
Across the continent, in a bright flash, Zed Trice appears before Ha’Ven Maktar in his cell. He insists that Ha’Ven put on the gauntlet. They discuss long into the night, but what was said is unknown.
1772-08-01

scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/3 - The Great War/1772-08-01.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/3---the-great-war/.content:
Ha’Ven Maktar is suspended in chains, as his father comes arrives with Zed Trice and Flea McCallister. Disappointed in his son still refusing, attempts to claim the gauntlet for himself. Dyxe
stops him, freeing Ha’Ven. Ha’Ven puts on the gauntlet.
Dmascus orders Ha’Ven be brought to the entrance of the city with Zed Trice. The first of the KOA forces arrive, Wulfs, Bhats, Wizro, and a Titan named Arlo “The Pugilist” Comstock. Zed Trice joins him, defying Dmascus with a middle finger.
Samuel Wibblebrook rallies the KOA behind the loss of their Consulate. The construction of the giant Nova Generator will be ready in 4 days.
Aberdine Salazar Abacus makes his way north. Hiding in caves during the day studying the tomes, and moving by night.
After defending the capital, Ha Ven and Zed camp for the night. They are then met by Creed Billingstone, who offers assistance for a fee.
1772-08-02

scars-of-kalakar/politics/goverment/arbo.content: The belief that no land is owned, but borrowed, all are equal and free. None shall put a hand on another, to chill ones speak, or to interfere with the pursuit of happiness.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/cul.title: Cult of Ha'Ven
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/cul.content:
A cult that worships the heroism of Ha’Ven Maktar. They believe he guides their way through his unfettered guidance, and was a Martyr in the Great War, and he has risen again to end their fear. They see his father, and those who follow Abacus as heathens who follow the ego and selfishness. 
They make public shrines to him by remaking his sword out of scrap and lighting it on fire.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/emp.title: Empirialist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/emp.content: Kalakains who believe they are the true ruling class. All others are for the benefit of the elites.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/fra.title: Fraternist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/fra.content: The general belief that everyone has a role in society.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/iso.title: Isolationist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/iso.content: The belief that each race should never coincide socially, with the exception of bartering. No money as that incorporates other cultures.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/pro.title: Proclivist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/pro.content: The general belief that some races are different classes in society based on intelligence, economic productivity.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/the.title: Theocratic
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/the.content: ruled by a king—the pharaoh—who was viewed as a living god and the high religious leader.

We believe knowledge becomes most powerful when it is free, shared, and accessible to everyone. Open access fuels creativity, equality, and collective progress, and it helps every visitor learn, grow, and contribute to something bigger than themselves.
This Knowledge Center is your starting point for exploring both the Scars of Kalakar universe and a broader digital garden of game development, art, and media resources.
